query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A predictive model that explicitly incorporates atomic-level chemical short-range order and lattice distortion effects—derived from cluster expansion and Monte Carlo simulations—will more accurately identify high-entropy alloys with exceptionally low phonon thermal conductivity for thermal-insulation applications compared to models based solely on bulk composition averages.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) synthesized as random solid solutions exhibiting intrinsic chemical disorder and lattice distortions.
generation.intervention: Application of a predictive algorithm that integrates ab initio cluster expansion methods, combined with Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations to capture local chemical fluctuations and dual-porosity effects.
generation.conditions: Ambient to moderate temperatures (e.g., 300–700 K) under conditions typical for thermal-insulation performance tests. Samples are prepared under controlled annealing conditions to stabilize the desired disordered microstructure.
generation.structural_mediator: Local chemical short-range order and the dual-porosity microstructure which together induce severe lattice distortions.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced lattice distortions increase phonon scattering and reduce phonon mean free paths. By accurately modeling the chemical ordering and local structural variations, the predictive approach should capture the critical physics that control phonon transport, leading to lower thermal conductivity than predicted by traditional bulk-composition-based models.
generation.predicted_outcome: Candidate HEAs identified by the predictive model will show a statistically significant reduction in phonon thermal conductivity (e.g., improved prediction accuracy by at least 15-20% relative to conventional methods) during thermal performance testing.
generation.baseline: Traditional predictive methods that rely primarily on averaged compositional descriptors and empirical correlations, which typically underestimate the impact of local chemical fluctuations and porous microstructures on phonon scattering.
generation.boundary: The approach is expected to apply only to high-entropy alloys where significant chemical disorder and associated lattice distortions are present. It may not be applicable to alloys that have undergone ordering transformations or those with negligible local chemical variation.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative improvements in prediction remain uncertain due to potential variations in synthesis conditions and the scaling of dual-porosity effects on phonon dynamics, as well as the challenge of capturing non-equilibrium local ordering in simulations.

falsification_experiment.design: Select a statistically significant set of HEA compositions predicted by both the new predictive model and a conventional model. Synthesize samples under identical processing conditions and measure their lattice thermal conductivity using inelastic neutron scattering and complementary thermal diffusivity measurements across a temperature range (300–700 K). Compare the measured thermal conductivity values with the predictions from both models.
measurements: Lattice thermal conductivity (via inelastic neutron/X-ray scattering)
Thermal diffusivity and specific heat (to extract conductivity values)
Quantitative analysis of local chemical ordering using techniques such as atom-probe tomography or high-resolution TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEAs identified by the new predictive model do not consistently exhibit a thermal conductivity reduction that is at least 15–20% greater than that of compounds identified by traditional methods (or if no statistically significant difference is observed), then the hypothesis that the integrated predictive model provides superior identification of low-thermal-conductivity HEAs would be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The unique properties of the porous HECs are ascribed to the high-entropy effects and dual-porosity structures. The severe lattice distortions in the HECs lead to the low intrinsic thermal conductivity by reducing phonons’ mean free path and increasing phonon scattering. Moreover, this results in high compressive strength by inhibiting the crack generations and propagations. The dual-porosity structure possesses several small pores in high-porosity ceramics. These small pores are more efficient in scattering phonon thermal conductivity and inhibiting crack propagations, which are beneficial to improving the thermal insulation and mechanical properties of the porous HECs.

cited_evidence.kind: web:Origin of Cr- and V-rich precipitates in the HEAs
cited_evidence.text: To understand the origin of the Cr- and V-rich precipitates observed in annealed and irradiated HEA samples, we have systematically carried out first-principles calculations of phase stability and chemical short-range order (SRO) of the multicomponent 38 at % W/36 at % Ta/15 at % Cr/11 at % V alloy as a function of temperature. The cluster expansion (CE) methodology [see Methods and refs. ()] has been used to build up an ab initio–based Hamiltonian with many-body effective cluster interactions (ECIs), from which the configurational entropy and therefore the free energy of multicomponent system can be obtained from thermodynamic integration techniques () in combination with canonical Monte Carlo (CMC) simulations. The enthalpies of mixing were calculated using the density functional theory (DFT) and CE methods for nearly 270 structures within the BCC underlying crystalline lattice. Values for all binary structures in the database were analyzed to determine the nature of the atomic interactions in all possible binary configurations (fig. S7). The positive and negative enthalpies of mixing values indicate a tendency for segregation or ordering, respectively.

cited_evidence.kind: web:3.5. Lattice Thermal Conductivity of PbSnTeSe
cited_evidence.text: Using the same approach, the value of κL was computed for various temperatures in the range 300–700 K (Figure 9). At 300 K, the κL value is 0.4 W K−1 m−1, which is a very low value of the lattice thermal conductivity, favorable for thermoelectric materials. This is due to the lattice distortion effect of high-entropy alloys that can reduce phonon velocity and enhance phonon scattering, resulting in low thermal conductivity. Additionally, one can observe that when the temperature rises, the thermal conductivity of the lattice decreases, which is also due to an increase in phonon scattering at higher temperatures.
